questions.stem: This chest radiograph shows a large thoracic aortic aneurysm with prominent aortic arch. If this patient develops new hoarseness, stretching or compression of which nerve is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Left vagus nerve trunk in the neck

explanation.summary: Because the left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the aortic arch, an expanding arch aneurysm stretches it, paralyzing the left vocal cord and producing hoarseness (Ortner cardiovocal syndrome).
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under the aortic arch, an expanding arch aneurysm stretches it, paralyzing the left vocal cord and producing hoarseness (Ortner cardiovocal syndrome).

questions.stem: Based on this diagram of thoracic lymphatic drainage, where does the large collecting vessel that drains most of the body empty into the venous system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Junction of the right jugular and right subclavian veins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Junction of the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superior vena cava at its midpoint

explanation.summary: The thoracic duct drains lymph from below the diaphragm and the left upper body, emptying at the left venous angle. The right lymphatic duct drains only the right head, neck, arm, and thorax into the right venous angle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The thoracic duct drains lymph from below the diaphragm and the left upper body, emptying at the left venous angle. The right lymphatic duct drains only the right head, neck, arm, and thorax into the right venous angle.

questions.stem: According to this diagram of body lymphatic drainage territories, lymph from the right arm, right side of the head/neck, and right thorax drains through which vessel?

explanation.summary: The right upper quadrant of the body (right head/neck, right arm, right thorax) drains via the short right lymphatic duct into the right venous angle; the remaining three quadrants drain via the thoracic duct.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right upper quadrant of the body (right head/neck, right arm, right thorax) drains via the short right lymphatic duct into the right venous angle; the remaining three quadrants drain via the thoracic duct.

questions.stem: This anterior view of the thoracic wall veins highlights the azygos and hemiazygos system. What is the principal functional role of this venous system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It provides collateral drainage between the superior and inferior vena cava

choices.label: B
choices.text: It drains the myocardium directly into the right atrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: It supplies arterial blood to the intercostal muscles

choices.label: D
choices.text: It delivers portal blood to the liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: It carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium

explanation.summary: The azygos/hemiazygos veins collect posterior intercostal and mediastinal blood and connect the IVC and SVC territories, serving as a critical collateral pathway when either cava is obstructed.
explanation.whyCorrect: The azygos/hemiazygos veins collect posterior intercostal and mediastinal blood and connect the IVC and SVC territories, serving as a critical collateral pathway when either cava is obstructed.

questions.stem: This diagram of the thoracic aorta and its branches shows the ligamentum arteriosum near the arch. This fibrous cord is the postnatal remnant of which fetal structure?

explanation.summary: The ligamentum arteriosum is the obliterated ductus arteriosus, which in fetal life shunted blood from the pulmonary trunk to the aorta, bypassing the lungs. The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ligamentum arteriosum is the obliterated ductus arteriosus, which in fetal life shunted blood from the pulmonary trunk to the aorta, bypassing the lungs. The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around it.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the thoracic splanchnic nerves arising from the sympathetic trunk. From which spinal cord segments do the preganglionic fibers of the greater splanchnic nerve originate?

explanation.summary: The greater splanchnic nerve carries preganglionic sympathetic fibers from T5-T9. The lesser (T10-T11) and least (T12) splanchnic nerves arise from lower thoracic segments, together supplying abdominal viscera.
explanation.whyCorrect: The greater splanchnic nerve carries preganglionic sympathetic fibers from T5-T9. The lesser (T10-T11) and least (T12) splanchnic nerves arise from lower thoracic segments, together supplying abdominal viscera.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph is paired with drained pleural fluid shown as milky-white bottles. What is this fluid, and what does it indicate?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Frank blood from a lacerated intercostal artery (hemothorax)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cerebrospinal fluid from a dural tear

explanation.summary: The characteristic milky, triglyceride-rich appearance identifies chyle. Chylothorax results from thoracic duct injury or obstruction (trauma, surgery, malignancy such as lymphoma).
explanation.whyCorrect: The characteristic milky, triglyceride-rich appearance identifies chyle. Chylothorax results from thoracic duct injury or obstruction (trauma, surgery, malignancy such as lymphoma).

questions.stem: This case shows a milky pericardial/pleural effusion (jar of white fluid) associated with an anterior mediastinal mass. Disruption of which structure best explains this milky fluid?

explanation.summary: Milky, triglyceride-rich fluid (chyle) accumulates when the thoracic duct is obstructed or lacerated, most often by tumor or surgery, producing chylothorax or chylopericardium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Milky, triglyceride-rich fluid (chyle) accumulates when the thoracic duct is obstructed or lacerated, most often by tumor or surgery, producing chylothorax or chylopericardium.

questions.stem: This sagittal CT shows a mass in the compartment behind the heart and aorta (posterior mediastinum). Which category of tumor is most characteristic of this location?

explanation.summary: Posterior mediastinal masses arise near the sympathetic chain and spinal nerves, so neurogenic tumors predominate. Thymoma, teratoma, and thyroid masses are anterior mediastinal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Posterior mediastinal masses arise near the sympathetic chain and spinal nerves, so neurogenic tumors predominate. Thymoma, teratoma, and thyroid masses are anterior mediastinal.

questions.stem: This illustration of esophageal lymphatic drainage shows nodes along the entire esophagus. Why does esophageal carcinoma frequently produce widely scattered (skip) nodal metastases?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Esophageal lymph drains exclusively to a single sentinel node

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lymph flows only downward toward the celiac nodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: The esophagus has no lymphatic drainage, so tumor spreads only hematogenously

choices.label: D
choices.text: The esophagus has an extensive, longitudinally interconnected submucosal lymphatic plexus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Metastases occur only after direct invasion of the aorta

explanation.summary: The rich, longitudinally oriented submucosal lymphatic network of the esophagus permits tumor cells to travel long distances before exiting to regional nodes, producing unpredictable skip metastases and complicating surgical staging.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rich, longitudinally oriented submucosal lymphatic network of the esophagus permits tumor cells to travel long distances before exiting to regional nodes, producing unpredictable skip metastases and complicating surgical staging.

questions.stem: This diagram of thoracic autonomic innervation shows the greater splanchnic nerve descending through the thorax. These preganglionic sympathetic fibers pass through the sympathetic chain without synapsing and instead synapse at which ganglion?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Superior mesenteric artery ganglion of the vagus

explanation.summary: Greater splanchnic fibers (T5-T9) traverse the sympathetic chain without synapsing and synapse in the celiac (prevertebral) ganglion, supplying sympathetic innervation to foregut structures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Greater splanchnic fibers (T5-T9) traverse the sympathetic chain without synapsing and synapse in the celiac (prevertebral) ganglion, supplying sympathetic innervation to foregut structures.
